data.title: Watcher hardening nits from AS-7 review (lock steal race, sentinel tmp suffix, SIGKILL timer)

data.body: Backlog-grade findings from the AS-7 review (none violate a stated criterion; all bounded-consequence). (1) acquireLock stale-steal race: two actors that both observe a stale advance.lock can interleave unlink+create so both believe they hold it — reachable only when a manual/loop tick steals the same >=45min-stale lock in the same instant as the watcher; plan §5 declares the lock etiquette-not-correctness, so this is sanctioned residual risk. Hardening: after wx-create, re-read the lock and confirm pid==self. (2) Sentinel tmp file uses a fixed name (last-human-message.json.tmp); two store processes (server container + CLI container share the bind mount) can interleave write/rename so one rename ENOENTs (caught) or the sentinel briefly holds the lower messageId — never torn, never loses a message (inbox sweep + sentinel>highwater re-trigger); verified with a 2x200-post concurrent hammer (valid JSON, zero tmp orphans). Hardening: unique tmp suffix (pid+random). (3) advance-watcher.mjs SIGKILL grace timer closes over the mutable 'child' variable; with default config unreachable, but if ADVANCE_DEBOUNCE_S is set below the fixed 15s kill grace, a timed-out tick's SIGKILL timer can kill a just-spawned successor tick (consequence: one wasted tick, logged, next message retries). Hardening: clear the kill timer in the exit handler or capture the child in the closure. Also cosmetic: SKIP log line every poll while a foreign lock is held with a pending sentinel (~360 lines per 30min loop tick, bounded by 5MiB rotation); pid-guard read-then-write TOCTOU for two simultaneously started manual watchers (launchd + fire-time wx lock make it moot).

PLAN (cto-owen): triage of Priya's five AS-7 findings. FIX 1-4: (1) verify-after-create in acquireLock (shrinks double-steal, lock stays etiquette — explicitly not eliminated); (2) unique sentinel tmp suffix pid+random in store.js writeHumanSentinel, best-effort orphan unlink; (3) capture spawned child in a per-fire const + clear SIGKILL grace timer on exit; (4) SKIP log dedupe per episode, mirroring lastBadSentinel pattern. WON'T-FIX 5: pid-guard TOCTOU — courtesy guard, launchd + fire-time wx lock bound it; one-line sanctioning comment only. Preferred lift: makeLockOps exported from watcher for fs-backed in-container tests (mountless invariant holds; fs-in-tempdir fine). Tests extend store.test.js + watcher.test.js; suite via docker compose, no real claude spawns. Est: small — ~40 lines code, ~80 lines tests.

IMPL (developer-marcus): all four fixes + won't-fix comment landed in 89e8557. (1) makeLockOps lifted+exported per plan's preferred shape — verify-after-create yields without unlink on foreign pid; injectables (pid, isPidAlive, readFile) added for the fs-backed tests, defaults are the real collaborators. (2) sentinel tmp = path.pid.rand.tmp, orphan unlink in the catch. (3) per-fire proc capture, shared settle() clears both timers, child===proc guard. (4) SKIP once per episode, '(suppressing repeats)' suffix on the first line. (5) pid-guard comment only. Deviations, all boring: store failure-injection test reworked to squat the sentinel path with a directory (old .tmp squat can't collide with unique names — it would have passed vacuously); that same test now proves orphan cleanup after a failed rename. Pinned the existing unparsable-lock steal path in tests alongside dead-pid/age. Container suite 83 pass / 0 fail (was 78); main() never executes under test; no watcher run against the live system.

REVIEW (qa-priya, cold): PASS — recommend done, no rework, no inline fixes needed. Reviewed 89e8557 via git diff master...feat/AS-13-watcher-hardening against plan dispositions; my AS-7 findings are the yardstick. Suite re-run myself in-container (DOCKER_BUILDKIT=1 COMPOSE_DOCKER_CLI_BUILD=1 docker compose run --rm --build test): 83 pass / 0 fail, matching the claim (+5 over AS-7's 78: 4 makeLockOps, 1 two-store interleave). FINDINGS vs FIXES: (1) lock steal race — CLOSED as scoped: verify-after-create in makeLockOps returns false without unlink on foreign pid; I re-ran my original interleave in-container (stale dead-pid lock, B unlink+create injected exactly between A's wx-create and verify): A.acquire=false, STEAL-LOST logged, lock stays B's (pid 222) through A's releaseLock. Residual double-fire when A verifies before B strikes remains and remains sanctioned per the etiquette stance — comment in acquireLock says exactly that, honestly. (2) tmp collision — CLOSED: pid+random suffix, orphan unlink in catch; re-ran my 2x200 two-process hammer in-container: messageId=400, exact 4-field contract, zero tmp orphans. (3) SIGKILL timer — CLOSED: both timers and both handlers close over per-fire proc; settle() clears termTimer+killTimer and nulls child iff child===proc. No handler references mutable child except the sanctioned gate. (4) SKIP spam — CLOSED: lastSkipKey on reason:messageId, reset on any non-skip action, '(suppressing repeats)' on first line; walked poll(): new messageId, reason change, or any observed lock release starts a new episode (a release+reacquire entirely between 5s polls is unobservable — inherent, fine). (5) pid-guard TOCTOU — WON'T-FIX comment present at the guard, honest ('bounds the damage to log noise' — matches my AS-7 assessment). ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA: 1 pass (foreign-pid yield no-unlink + own-pid true tested; dead-pid/age/unparsable steal behavior unchanged and now pinned), 2 pass (readdir sweeps on success and failed-rename paths; contract test intact), 3 pass (logs byte-identical at defaults except the (4) suffix; STEAL-LOST only reachable in the race that previously double-fired silently), 4 pass, 5 pass (comment only, guard logic untouched), 6 pass (83/83 mountless, main() never ran — no START lines, no watcher process, no live-system touches, no claude spawns). DEVIATIONS all sound: sentinel-path-squat rework is strictly stronger (old .tmp-dir squat would pass vacuously against unique names; new shape also proves orphan cleanup); injectables (pid/isPidAlive/readFile) with production defaults are the minimal seam the plan invited; unparsable-lock steal pin is pure added coverage of behavior criterion 1 requires unchanged. Traced and accepted, not filed: verify-read-null branch yields conservatively (stranding own lock requires an unreadable own-write; ENOENT case leaves nothing stranded, and 45min age-stale self-recovers). Nothing rises to backlog.
